lina: Customer reporting repeated 503s when calling /v1/generate and very high tail latency (>5s). They supplied a request id but no repro yet. Asking for minimal repro snippets (curl/py/js/go) + what logs/request headers we need.
jamal: Can you paste the request-id they gave? we can search logs and check upstreams.
customer-tech: request-id: req_2026-03-16-9a1b2c3d. Happened ~2026-03-16T18:12Z. Happened on hosted-redwood-us-west region.
lina: thx. First steps: can you run a single curl that reproduces the call (copy exact headers + payload). If you can't reproduce, we need a tiny SDK snippet for py/js/go we can run locally. Also need a minimal debug bundle: response headers (x-request-id, x-rlimit, x-server-timing), client logs showing timings, and any proxy/nginx logs.
maria: Minimal curl we ask for (customer):
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_2026-03-16-9a1b2c3d" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-mini-1","input":"Hello world","max_tokens":64}'
```
devx: For SDKs, we accept 3 tiny samples. keep them single-shot, no retries, and include explicit header injection for X-Request-ID. Ask the customer to run and paste stderr/stdout.
jamal: Python minimal (requests):
```python
import os, requests
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
headers = {
    'Authorization': f"Bearer {os.environ.get('REDWOOD_KEY')}",
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'X-Request-ID': 'req_2026-03-16-9a1b2c3d'
}
payload = {"model":"redwood-mini-1","input":"hello","max_tokens":32}
r = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=10)
print('status', r.status_code)
print('headers', dict(r.headers))
print('body', r.text)
```
maria: JS (node fetch):
```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch')
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}` ,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'X-Request-ID': 'req_2026-03-16-9a1b2c3d'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({model:'redwood-mini-1', input:'hello', max_tokens:32}),
    timeout: 10000
  })
  console.log('status', res.status)
  console.log('headers', Object.fromEntries(res.headers))
  console.log('body', await res.text())
})()
```
devx: Go (net/http):
```go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "os"
  "io/ioutil"
)
func main() {
  payload := []byte(`{"model":"redwood-mini-1","input":"hello","max_tokens":32}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", bytes.NewBuffer(payload))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  req.Header.Set("X-Request-ID", "req_2026-03-16-9a1b2c3d")
  client := &http.Client{}
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err != nil { fmt.Println("err", err); return }
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  b, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println("status", resp.StatusCode)
  fmt.Println("headers", resp.Header)
  fmt.Println("body", string(b))
}
```

lina: From infra side we'll look for server logs for req_2026-03-16-9a1b2c3d. ops-bot: Searching logs... :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ops-bot: Found 3 entries across front-proxy and inference pool at 2026-03-16T18:12:07Z: 
```
[front-proxy] req=req_2026-03-16-9a1b2c3d status=503 upstr_latency_ms=4200 route=generate-01
[inference-pool/node-7] req=req_2026-03-16-9a1b2c3d error=kv-cache-miss duration_ms=4180
[model-worker/worker-3] req=req_2026-03-16-9a1b2c3d trace="oom-gradual-fallback" duration_ms=4175
```

maria: That stack suggests worker OOM triggered fallback and request timed out at proxy. Ask customer to confirm payload sizes, whether they used a long prompt/embeddings, and whether they saw increased memory on their side.
customer-tech: they were sending a ~30k token prompt via a single request (we now suspect this). I'll run the minimal scripts with the same prompt but truncated and post results.
lina: Perfect. If they can reproduce, request the full debug bundle: curl -v output, SDK stdout, client timings, and any NAT/proxy logs. Also ask for a k8s pod name or region so infra can fetch worker metrics.
jamal: Follow-up: I'll create a quick playbook snippet for the oncall to grep logs by X-Request-ID and check worker OOMs. Adding to the thread. :white_check_mark:
